skills.name: compute_chow_ring_of_projective_space
skills.description: Compute the Chow ring of a projective space by using the standard generator of divisor classes and the relation given by the top power.
skills.preconditions: A projective space of any dimension is given.
skills.postconditions: An explicit presentation of the Chow ring as a polynomial ring modulo the top-degree relation.
skills.example: For the projective line, the Chow ring is ℤ[h]/(h²) where h is the class of a point.

skills.name: translate_tangency_to_dual_incidence
skills.description: Express a tangency condition between two plane curves as an incidence condition in the dual projective plane.
skills.preconditions: Two plane curves are given, at least one of which is smooth, and the dual map is defined.
skills.postconditions: A subvariety of the dual plane representing lines tangent to the smooth curve is obtained.
skills.example: The set of lines tangent to a smooth cubic in the plane corresponds to a curve of degree six in the dual plane.

skills.name: construct_incidence_scheme
skills.description: Form an incidence scheme parametrising tuples that satisfy a list of geometric constraints and compute its expected dimension by subtracting codimensions.
skills.preconditions: A product of parameter spaces and a list of algebraic conditions are given.
skills.postconditions: A closed subscheme defined by the conditions together with its expected dimension.
skills.example: The incidence scheme of a line meeting a fixed point and a fixed conic in the plane has expected dimension zero.

skills.name: apply_generic_finiteness_of_projection
skills.description: Deduce that the projection from an incidence scheme to a subset of its factors is finite over a dense open locus where the fibers have the expected dimension zero.
skills.preconditions: An incidence scheme with a projection map is given, and the expected fiber dimension is zero.
skills.postconditions: Identification of an open subset of the base over which the projection is finite.
skills.example: Projecting the scheme of pairs (line, point) with the point on the line onto the space of lines is finite over the open set of lines not passing through a fixed point.

skills.name: use_etale_local_isomorphism_for_fiber_count
skills.description: When a morphism is étale over a point, replace the fiber by a disjoint union of copies of the base field to count geometric points.
skills.preconditions: A morphism is known to be étale at a rational point of the base.
skills.postconditions: The number of geometric points in the fiber equals the degree of the morphism at that point.
skills.example: An étale double cover of a smooth curve has exactly two points over each rational point of the base.

skills.name: apply_lefschetz_fixed_point_formula
skills.description: Relate the count of rational points of a smooth proper variety over a finite field to traces of Frobenius on its cohomology.
skills.preconditions: A smooth proper variety over a finite field is given.
skills.postconditions: An expression for the point count as a sum of alternating traces of Frobenius.
skills.example: For a smooth projective curve of genus g, the number of 𝔽_q‑points equals q + 1 – Σ_{i=1}^{2g} α_i where the α_i are Frobenius eigenvalues.

skills.name: use_chebotarev_density_for_average_fiber_size
skills.description: Estimate the average size of fibers of a finite morphism by applying Chebotarev density to the distribution of Frobenius conjugacy classes.
skills.preconditions: A finite, generically étale morphism of varieties over a number field is given.
skills.postconditions: An asymptotic formula for the average number of points in fibers over finite fields of increasing size.
skills.example: For a degree‑three covering of the projective line, the average number of points in fibers over 𝔽_p tends to three as p → ∞.

skills.name: apply_birational_invariance_of_chow_classes
skills.description: Replace a variety by a birational model without changing its Chow class computations for cycles of codimension one.
skills.preconditions: Two varieties are birational and a divisor class on one is to be computed.
skills.postconditions: The divisor class can be computed on the simpler birational model.
skills.example: A blow‑up of the plane at a point is birational to the plane; the class of the exceptional divisor pulls back to the class of a point.

skills.name: compute_intersection_number_via_schubert_calculus
skills.description: Calculate a top‑degree intersection product in a Grassmannian or flag variety using Schubert classes and their multiplication rules.
skills.preconditions: An intersection problem is expressed in terms of Schubert cycles in a homogeneous space.
skills.postconditions: A numerical intersection number obtained by expanding the product in the Schubert basis.
skills.example: In the Grassmannian of lines in three‑space, the product of two Schubert classes of codimension one equals the class of a point, giving intersection number one.

skills.name: deduce_asymptotic_average_from_point_counts
skills.description: Derive the limiting average of a quantity defined via point counts over finite fields by taking the ratio of sums and applying a limit as the field size grows.
skills.preconditions: A sequence of finite sets indexed by prime powers with known cardinalities is given.
skills.postconditions: The limit of the average value of a function on those sets is obtained.
skills.example: If the number of solutions to a polynomial equation over 𝔽_q is q + O(1), then the average number of solutions per field element tends to one as q → ∞.
